strengths: Line-as-address (living along the Keio, listings as geography) is something Japanese readers would recognize
Private terminals as commercial territory, landmark transfers, and fare-grumbling-while-tapping feel local rather than tourism copy
Avoids invented first-person memoir; uses 'many children' / 'some people… others…' hedges

issues.location: ## How Japanese People Live Inside the Patchwork
issues.problem: 'Staff answer with company names first: JR, Metro, Keio—not “the subway” as a single object' over-scripts a typical interaction. Staff often start from destination, ticket, or gate.
issues.suggestion: Hedge: staff often need the company or line name, because 'the subway' is not one object in a stacked hub.

issues.location: ## Why So Many Companies Were Allowed to Remain (station design)
issues.problem: Locals do not experience door queues or escalator sides as consequences of operator plurality. Those habits sit on crowding and timetables.
issues.suggestion: Do not explain platform manners as adaptations to a multi-operator city.
